correctness.rationale: For all a,b,u,v>0 and d>=0, the drift has a strictly positive definite stability matrix. The exact 3x3 Lyapunov solution yields V(d), and the derivative and threshold ratio have independently checked multivariate integer-polynomial identities. The ratio derivative has sign(a-b) everywhere d>=0, while V' has sign(a-b)*sign(R-v/u), proving a strict minimum iff the ratio is inside the endpoint window and excluding maxima. Matched u=a,v=b gives V=1-d(a-b)^2/[2(s+2d)(ab+sd)], the unique optimizer sqrt(ab/2), and an exact positivity certificate for V>1/2; the bound is approached as b/a tends to infinity. The bundled verifier passes symbolic identities and 288 independent rational Lyapunov solutions; finite tests are supplemental, not substitutes for the real-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The regional sum variance is a natural ecological measure of fluctuations, directly connected to dispersal and heterogeneity mechanisms in 2006–2015 metapopulation literature. The theorem solves the complete two-patch fixed-noise symmetric-dispersal optimization over all positive rates: a sharp noise-ratio phase interval, uniqueness/no maximum, a natural equal-isolated-variance calibration with explicit optimum, and a sharp uniform limiting performance bound. These precise boundaries are ecologically motivated and not merely a numerical scan or renaming of a known covariance formula; 2015 heterogeneous metapopulation diagrams lack an all-rate threshold for this model. Results are limited to the specified OU system and are not passed off as empirical extinction predictions.
